journey.title: Find what an agent cannot call, and why
journey.purpose: The day-one journey. Before a single program has run, an operator can already learn the shape of the acting surface: what is callable, what is not, and which of the closed set of reasons explains each gap. It ends pointing at the work that would raise the ceiling.

steps.intent: Arrive with nothing run yet, learn what a program and a handle are, and see that binding coverage is reported even though the corpus is empty.
Browse the resolved namespace and see bound capabilities against their denominator rather than as a standalone inventory.
Filter to the unbound capabilities and read the reason attached to each one.
Recognise that the largest single reason is scenarios shipping no CLI manifest at all, which is the hard ceiling on everything the runtime can do.
Confirm the same coverage is published as a declared measure, so the finding is answerable through search-hub by anyone who never opens this console.

claims.statement: Every step completes with zero programs submitted and zero sessions live.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-007's promotion argument. If this journey needs history, the binding registry belongs back at P2.

claims.statement: The journey ends with each unbound capability attributed to a named reason and an owning scenario.
claims.rationale: An unattributed gap cannot be assigned to anyone, which makes the Act projection a scoreboard rather than a work queue.

claims.statement: The coverage finding is reachable as a declared measure, not only as a rendered page.
claims.rationale: The primary user never opens this UI. A finding that exists only on screen is invisible to the agents and teams that would act on it.
